title: Observe where a remote SSH connection leads on macOS and Linux, so off-worktree proxies there stop counting in every worktree
outcome: On macOS and Linux the connection observer in src/engram_host_identity.rs reads no table (engram_tcp_connections returns None, EngramProcess::is_running is false), so every remote proxy in a turn whose workdir lies in no local worktree counts in every worktree there. That is the safe direction but it withholds credit on those hosts while any proxy is mid-turn. Add an observer for those platforms with the same rule as Windows: the transport's live ssh child owns exactly one outbound TCP connection besides its -L forward, to an address this machine does not hold (for example /proc/net/tcp plus /proc/<pid>/fd on Linux, proc_pidinfo/proc_pidfdinfo on macOS), with injected-table tests.
acceptance: On Linux and on macOS, a remote whose live ssh child owns exactly one outbound connection to a non-local address is classified as another machine, every other case stays maybe this machine, and platform tests with an injected table cover it.
